assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states at the magic angle opened an entirely new experimental platform, a door to phenomena nobody could see or tune before. The original experiment is clean and the field it launched is large and still productive.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the flat bands and the magic angle, and the Jarillo-Herrero group made the original experimental observation. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment prize configuration. Fair credit for device fabrication and early independent confirmations should be checked against the historical record.
assessment.maturity: The results have been reproduced by many independent groups across several moire systems in under a decade. The core observations are stable, though the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: Mechanism of moire superconductivity remains unsettled.
Credit for the experimental work may extend to co-authors and the early Cory Dean group work on related moire systems; I am not able to verify this independently.
Whether the field is old enough for the committee's usual standards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators are a landmark discovery in condensed matter. The quantum spin Hall state was observed experimentally in HgTe wells and three-dimensional topological insulators were confirmed by photoemission. The impact on understanding of matter and on spintronics and quantum devices is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction. Molenkamp's group made the original experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect, and Hasan's group did the first 3D topological insulator observation. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, and Fu and Kane, Moore and Balents, and Roy also contributed. They are not credited here, so the allocation of credit is a real problem. I would credit the decisive experiments and the foundational theory.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently many times over nearly two decades. Timely or even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between several theorists and between the 2D and 3D experiments is unresolved.
Kane-Mele and Mele are separated if only three names are used; Eugene J. Mele is left out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and its experimental realisation, brought clock stability beyond the caesium standard by orders of magnitude. A new measurement tool that opens doors to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and the redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and made the first strontium demonstrations. Jun Ye's group pushed the performance to the extreme. The pair is a compact and defensible configuration, though Hall and Hänsch were already recognised in 2005 for the frequency comb, and others (e.g. Ludlow, Lemonde, Takamoto) contributed to the maturation.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs have reproduced the clocks. The redefinition of the SI second is not yet complete, so societal impact is still ahead of us.
uncertainties: Whether Katori's early proposal or the later performance demonstrations should dominate the credit.
Possible overlap in the committee's mind with earlier clock-related prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spherical-aberration correction made it possible to image atoms in materials routinely at sub-angstrom resolution, an invention that changed how interfaces, defects and nanostructures are studied across physics, chemistry and materials science. This is a genuine new instrument that opened a door.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory of the corrector, Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the first working corrector on a TEM in 1998. Krivanek's STEM corrector work is a parallel and independently important contribution and is not in the supplied credit, so any prize configuration has a real allocation problem. As someone who works in this field I should say plainly that I have a conflict of interest and a possible bias towards this candidate, and I have tried to apply the same standard as for others.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with commercial instruments now ubiquitous. Recognition by other prizes has already happened, so timeliness is not a concern, but it can be questioned whether this is physics or an instrument prize adjacent to chemistry.
uncertainties: Krivanek and colleagues' parallel STEM correction work is not in the credited names.
My own conflict of interest as a practitioner.
Whether the committee would regard this as physics rather than methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of superconductivity at around 26 K in fluorine-doped LaFeAsO opened the second family of high-temperature superconductors and triggered a worldwide search. It is a clear original materials discovery by an experimental group.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 JACS paper by Kamihara, Hosono and co-authors is the original report, so a prize to the two credited names is clean. Subsequent increases in Tc in other groups (e.g. in China) were important follow-up and not the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and rapidly. The mechanism of pairing is still not settled and no Tc breakthrough for applications has followed, which tempers the impact argument.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is still debated.
Practical impact is more modest than the cuprates, which already were rewarded.
Roles of other Hosono-group members in the discovery are not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube built a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice and discovered a flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, opening neutrino astronomy as a new window, followed by the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic plane observation.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the project and its science case, Spiering and Karle were central to the design, construction and analysis. It is a large collaboration, and AMANDA and Baikal precursors, as well as many analysts, complicate credit. I cannot independently verify who made the decisive contributions to the 2013 discovery.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed with multiple channels and by follow-up multi-messenger observations, but the identification of the sources is still partial. Recognition is timely but the picture is still developing.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the roles of AMANDA and Baikal.
Source identification remains incomplete.
Possible preference for a more fully mature discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance of tens of percent, observed independently in 1995, made magnetic tunnel junctions practical and underlies hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It is an experiment that directly benefits society.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported the original room-temperature observations in 1995. Julliere's 1975 low-temperature result and Parkin's work on MgO-based giant TMR with Yuasa and Djayaprawira are separate parts of the compound story, and the Fert-Grunberg GMR prize in 2007 already covers adjacent ground. The prize configuration needs careful sorting of who did what first.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and commercially validated for more than two decades. Possibly overdue, though the closeness to the GMR prize is a concern.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize and Julliere's earlier work.
Whether the MgO giant TMR should be in the same prize as the 1995 room-temperature result.
Parkin's credit is left out of the proposed laureates here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed the mechanism for which the 2013 prize was awarded and is one of the great experimental achievements, requiring detectors and instruments of unprecedented scale. The importance for our understanding of the universe is beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: The theorists were recognised in 2013. For the experiment, the individual credit is hard because thousands of people made the discovery. Founding spokespersons and project leaders, Jenni, Della Negra and Virdee, conceived and led the detectors over decades, whereas Gianotti was spokesperson at the time of the announcement. Allocation is genuinely unresolved and I cannot verify it independently.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by two independent experiments and by subsequent coupling measurements. The only questions are about attribution and whether the Prize already covered it.
uncertainties: Only three of four credited names may be proposed.
Whether collaboration-scale discoveries fit the three-person limit.
Possible view that the 2013 prize already settled this topic.
